AI Use Policy

Martin Paul Eve
Professor of Literature, Technology and Publishing

This page sets out whether and how automated and artificial intelligence (AI) tools are used across this website, eve.gd. It applies to the whole site: blog posts, essays, my biography, the publications list, and any other content published here.

What is and is not written by AI

The textual content on this site is 100% human-written. I write my blog posts, essays, and biographical pages myself. These are not generated by AI tools. I do not draft with AI and I do not use AI correction tools.

I do use voice assistance tools (automated transcription), particularly when my rheumatoid arthritis makes typing too painful. These tools sometimes use AI systems for their transcription (such as the NVIDIA Parakeet nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2 model).

There is one significant piece of automation on the site. My publications list is populated automatically from the Birkbeck Institutional Repository (BIROn) through an automated feed, rather than being typed out by hand. This is the main place where an automated process contributes to what you see.

The Site & Policies pages listed in the footer (e.g. this page) were created from an amalgam of other policies on other sites around the web. AI may have been used on those pages.

The HTML and CSS code for this site were partially coded by hand and partially coded with AI assistance (Anthropic Claude Opus 4.8).

Where I use AI assistance for anything else published on the site, I disclose it. If I have not disclosed AI involvement on a given page, that page or post was written by me.

Scope, limitations, and safeguards

The specific tasks that may involve automation are: retrieving and formatting my list of publications from BIROn. Everything else is human work.

Automated output is checked by me before it appears on the site. The publications feed in particular is reviewed before it goes live, so that errors in metadata, classification, or formatting can be caught and corrected. I wrote the code that pulls this from BIROn and formats it into a PDF CV myself, by hand, back in the days before AI.

Oversight, review, and accountability

Automated and AI outputs on this site, including the auto-populated BIROn publications feed, are reviewed by a human before publication. That human is me, Martin Paul Eve.

The review process works like this: the automated feed proposes entries drawn from BIROn; I review those entries for accuracy and appropriateness; and only reviewed content is published. I am accountable for all content on this site, whether written by hand or drawn from an automated feed.

How the publications feed is ordered and audited

The publications list is ordered by date, with the newest items shown first. Each entry’s classification is auditable through the BIROn repository itself. In the list, a green download link indicates a green open-access accepted manuscript, and a gold link indicates a gold open-access version. Because the underlying records live in BIROn, the selection and the green-versus-gold classification of any item can be checked against the repository. There are sometimes some problems with the metadata, such as published items remaining in “In Press” status. I fix these as I notice them.

Coding of the site

Large language models have been used for programming in creating the structure and design of the site. In particular, I have used LLMs (Anthropic Claude Opus 4.8) to improve page metadata. As above, none of the blog content or other pages were written by AI.

Last reviewed: July 2026
